# Agent Plugins directory

> Curated directory of Agent Plugins, the open vendor-neutral standard that bundles Agent Skills and MCP servers into one portable drop-in folder every compliant client can read. Also tracks which clients actually support the standard today.

This repository has one data surface: `README.md`. There is no generated catalog file, no CSV and
no JSON feed here. Entries are markdown bullets under H2 headings, each carrying the entry name, its
repository link, the author and a one line description.

## Files

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-agent-plugins/main/README.md): the whole list. Headings cover what an Agent Plugin is, a build-your-first quickstart, the client support matrix, the catalog itself, skills and MCP servers not yet packaged as plugins, validation and scaffolding tools, and the spec resources.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-agent-plugins/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the bar an entry has to clear and the exact format a new entry uses.

## What the marks mean

- A catalog entry is listed only after its live `plugin.json` was fetched and found to carry the
  canonical 1.0.0 `$schema`. A per-client manifest that is not an Agent Plugin does not qualify, and
  a repository whose manifest cannot be fetched is not listed.
- In the client support matrix, `✅` means confirmed against that vendor's own documentation or
  announcement, `❌` means the vendor states it is not supported, and `❓` means not yet confirmed
  from a primary source. `❓` is a third state and never collapses into either of the other two.
  The matrix carries its own as-of date in the line directly above it.
- Every linked repository is re-resolved through the GitHub API weekly, which catches the renames
  and archives that a plain HTTP check passes clean. Links are swept for rot on the same cadence.
- This is a curated list, not a security review. Installing a plugin runs third-party code with the
  permissions of whoever installed it.

## How an agent should use this list

1. Fetch `README.md` once. It is a single file and it is the complete list.
2. For "does client X support Agent Plugins", read the client support matrix and carry its `❓`
   cells through as unconfirmed. Do not report an unconfirmed cell as a yes or a no.
3. Take install and validation commands verbatim from the fenced block beside the entry.
4. Quote the entry's own description and link to its source repository. Do not invent authors,
   licences, schema versions or install commands that are not in the file.
5. Ask the person before installing a plugin or handing it credentials.
6. To add or correct an entry, open a pull request against this repository. There is no write API
   and nothing here accepts a direct push.
